note: Set B is cleaner and captures the 7% outfitting mass allowance (plus 100 t transition piece) that Set A omits, while Set A pads its list with three duplicate pairs of the same steel properties restated with different number formatting. Set A also adds an unsupported 'typical variation' condition to the 20–30 m clearance claim from the footnote. Both sets bind the material, geometry, and frequency values correctly with supporting quotes, so B wins on fewer redundant/unsupported claims and better coverage of the mass note.
remarks: Set A repeats steel density, Young's modulus and shear modulus twice each (only the decimal formatting differs), inflating its count. Set B's 'final mass | outfitting mass' entity is somewhat vague (the subject is the final mass values in Table 1-1). Both sets leave the table's apparent unit error for soil Poisson's ratio (listed as Pa) unflagged; the 20–30 m clearance range in the footnote is captured only by A.
